Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Expectation2: Participate in project planning and provide accurate time estimates
Situation2: Management needs firm estimates for the quarterly roadmap and is awaiting their input
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was about to join the project planning call. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his voice tight with panic. “I think I left my passport at home. Can you check and bring it to the airport? My flight’s in two hours.” I glanced at the clock—management was waiting for my estimates, and the roadmap meeting was about to start. As the team’s engineer, everyone depended on my input to set realistic deadlines. Missing the call would throw off the whole schedule, and I knew how much pressure the company was under to deliver this quarter. But Sam had always been there for me, and I could hear the desperation in his voice. My mind raced, torn between the responsibility to my team and the loyalty to my friend. I stared at my laptop, the meeting invite blinking, while my keys sat on the table, ready to go. My heart pounded as I weighed the expectations pressing in from both sides, feeling the stress build as I realized I couldn’t possibly meet both demands at once.
